pages.text: A porphyry copper stock carries chalcopyrite with a little molybdenite, and the molybdenite carries rhenium at parts per million. Chalcopyrite roasted on a fire becomes a copper oxide the bloomery smelts to copper, the iron going to slag; bornite, chalcocite and covellite roast to a black copper calcine that does the same.
pages.title: The porphyry chain

pages.text: Two raw molybdenite roasted in a heated basin give two molybdenum trioxide, and half the time a rhenium flue dust: the roaster's flue is where every gram of the world's rhenium comes from.

Both oxides are reduced under hydrogen in a heated chemical vat with an industrial mixer, as the industry does: two trioxide and 500 mB of hydrogen give two molybdenum ingots, two flue dust and 250 mB give one rhenium ingot. Hydrogen is The Factory Must Grow's.
